newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Tuesday on a lack of market-moving news, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 8.86 percent from 9.15 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market plunged to 2.9 million lots from 6.2 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said there were only a few borrowers on the market today with no market-moving news in sight. A technical rebound on the stock markets also failed to lift the rates.
"Fund demand shrank sharply with market activity dropping sharply," said one trader.
Traders said another reason for Tuesday's dull trading was the recent downward trend in China's inflation rate, which is likely to exert pressure on the repo rates in the mid-term.
Traders said they expected the rates to rise slightly in the next few days due to a number of new issues on the domestic A share markets.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Tuesday on a technical rebound after falls in the past few trading days, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 120.16 yuan from 119.90 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market was thin at 746,651 lots, almost unchanged from 736,868 lots on Monday.
Traders said the technical rebound was supported by the high yields of some existing contracts but thin volume indicated market sentiment was still weak.
Traders said they believed the spot contracts would move narrowly around the current level in the next few days.
